source_text: וַֽ/יְהִ֗י כָּל נֶ֛פֶשׁ יֹצְאֵ֥י יֶֽרֶךְ יַעֲקֹ֖ב שִׁבְעִ֣ים נָ֑פֶשׁ וְ/יוֹסֵ֖ף הָיָ֥ה בְ/מִצְרָֽיִם־־׃
english_snapshot: And all the persons who came from Jacob’s loins[a] were seventy persons[b], and Joseph was already in Egypt.

signals.text: The Judean Desert manuscripts 4QGen-Exoda (4Q1) and 4QExodb (4Q13) support 'seventy-five'; in 4Q1, 'seventy' is reconstructed but 'and five' is preserved. The published transcription of 4QpaleoGen-Exodl (4Q11) reconstructs 'seventy' in a gap; the numeral itself is not preserved. 4Q13 proceeds directly to Joseph's death, omitting the clause, 'and Joseph was in Egypt.' The Septuagint has 'seventy-five' and places the Joseph clause before the total; the Samaritan Pentateuch agrees with the Masoretic 'seventy.'

source_text: וְ/לֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינ/וֹ֒ וַ/תִּֽקַּֽח ל/וֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַ/תַּחְמְרָ֥/ה בַ/חֵמָ֖ר וּ/בַ/זָּ֑פֶת וַ/תָּ֤שֶׂם בָּ/הּ֙ אֶת הַ/יֶּ֔לֶד וַ/תָּ֥שֶׂם בַּ/סּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַ/יְאֹֽר־־־־׃
english_snapshot: But when she could no longer hide him[a], she took for him a papyrus basket and coated it with bitumen and pitch. Then she put the child in it and placed it among the reeds by the bank of the Nile.

signals.text: Or 'a papyrus ark.' The Hebrew word tebah is the same word used for Noah's ark in Genesis, preserving a literary echo of deliverance through water.

source_text: וַ/יֵּ֨לֶךְ מֹשֶׁ֜ה וַ/יָּ֣שָׁב אֶל יֶ֣תֶר חֹֽתְנ֗/וֹ וַ/יֹּ֤אמֶר ל/וֹ֙ אֵ֣לֲכָה נָּ֗א וְ/אָשׁ֨וּבָה֙ אֶל אַחַ֣/י אֲשֶׁר בְּ/מִצְרַ֔יִם וְ/אֶרְאֶ֖ה הַ/עוֹדָ֣/ם חַיִּ֑ים וַ/יֹּ֧אמֶר יִתְר֛וֹ לְ/מֹשֶׁ֖ה לֵ֥ךְ לְ/שָׁלֽוֹם׀־־־׃
english_snapshot: Then Moses went and returned to Jethro his father-in-law and said to him[a], “Please let me go and return to my brothers who are in Egypt, so that I may see whether they are still alive.” And Jethro said to Moses[b], “Go in peace.”

signals.text: Hebrew has the name form 'Jether' in the first mention and 'Jethro' in the second; the English text uses 'Jethro' for consistency since the same person is clearly intended.

source_text: וּ/מוֹשַׁב֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשְׁב֖וּ בְּ/מִצְרָ֑יִם שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְ/אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָֽה׃
english_snapshot: The dwelling of the sons of Israel, who lived in Egypt[a], was four hundred thirty years.

signals.text: In 4QExodc (4Q14), the partly preserved name Egypt is followed directly by the duration, without the Septuagint's following reference to Canaan; the missing beginning cannot establish the wording of the whole clause. In 2QExoda (2Q2), the geographical phrase is reconstructed in a gap. The Samaritan Pentateuch reads, 'the dwelling of the sons of Israel and their fathers, which they lived in the land of Canaan and in the land of Egypt, was four hundred thirty years.' The Septuagint reads, 'the dwelling of the sons of Israel, which they lived in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, was four hundred thirty years.'

source_text: וַ/יֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֲנִ֛י חֹתֶנְ/ךָ֥ יִתְר֖וֹ בָּ֣א אֵלֶ֑י/ךָ וְ/אִ֨שְׁתְּ/ךָ֔ וּ/שְׁנֵ֥י בָנֶ֖י/הָ עִמָּֽ/הּ־׃
english_snapshot: He said to Moses[a], “I, Jethro your father-in-law, am coming to you, with your wife and her two sons with her.”

signals.text: Hebrew: 'her two sons.' Some English translations smooth this to 'your two sons,' but the Masoretic Text reads with a third feminine singular suffix, referring to Moses' wife.

source_text: אִם רָעָ֞ה בְּ/עֵינֵ֧י אֲדֹנֶ֛י/הָ אֲשֶׁר לא יְעָדָ֖/הּ וְ/הֶפְדָּ֑/הּ לְ/עַ֥ם נָכְרִ֛י לֹא יִמְשֹׁ֥ל לְ/מָכְרָ֖/הּ בְּ/בִגְד/וֹ בָֽ/הּ־־־־׃
english_snapshot: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master[a], who has not designated her for himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to a foreign people[b], since he has dealt deceitfully with her.

signals.text: Or, 'who has designated/betrothed her for himself.' The Hebrew clause is textually and interpretively difficult.

source_text: וְ/נָתַתָּ֤ה אֹת/וֹ֙ לִ/פְנֵ֣י הַ/פָּרֹ֔כֶת אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל אֲרֹ֣ן הָ/עֵדֻ֑ת לִ/פְנֵ֣י הַ/כַּפֹּ֗רֶת אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל הָ֣/עֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֛ר אִוָּעֵ֥ד לְ/ךָ֖ שָֽׁמָּ/ה־־׃
english_snapshot: And you shall place it before the veil that is before the ark of the testimony[a], before the mercy seat[b] that is over the testimony[c], where I will meet with you.

signals.text: The clause 'before the mercy seat that is over the testimony' is absent from the Samaritan Hebrew and the standard Septuagint text. The Samaritan text places these altar instructions after Exodus 26:35. The main text here retains the Masoretic wording and order.

source_text: וַ/יִּקַּ֣ח מִ/יָּדָ֗/ם וַ/יָּ֤צַר אֹת/וֹ֙ בַּ/חֶ֔רֶט וַֽ/יַּעֲשֵׂ֖/הוּ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַ/יֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨י/ךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּ/ךָ מֵ/אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
english_snapshot: And he took it from their hands and fashioned it with a graving tool[a], and he made it into a cast calf. Then they said, “These are your gods, Israel[d][c][b], who brought you up from the land of Egypt.”

signals.text: Some textual traditions read 'he said' instead of 'they said.'
